title: A Wreck for the Landfall
premise: Odile Coldharbour, a desert ranger chasing a thief named Vess Corrane across the salt flats, follows her to a cave the falling tide has exposed — inside it lies the wreck of the Meridian Lark, a ship impossibly far from any sea, and the inheritance Odile's dead mother hid there: proof that the salvage fleet's concession was forged. The fleet's enforcer, Harrow Quill, arrives to bury both ship and secret, and Odile must race six tides to raise the evidence before the permits expire and the wreck becomes fleet property forever. Betrayed by the debt he owes and the loyalty he owes it against, Odile finally chooses truth over the man who raised him — exposing Quill's forgery at the permit hearing as the tide closes for the last time.
about_author: Gideon Lockridge is a former coastal surveyor who spent eleven years mapping shorelines that no longer exist, and his fiction is haunted by things the water gives back. He writes from a houseboat he refuses to anchor in one place for longer than a season.

chapters.title: The Debt in the Dust
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Tracking Vess Corrane across the salt flats, Odile reflects on the debt binding him to her late father, who once saved his life. He catches her trail at a dried well. Emotional beat: duty worn like a yoke, resentment simmering under loyalty.

chapters.title: Six Tides of Nothing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The chase leads into country no map admits to — a basin that was seabed before the sea left. His compass spins uselessly. He finds Vess's camp abandoned mid-meal. Emotional beat: unease; the land itself is lying to him.

chapters.title: What the Tide Left
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A sound like breathing: an actual tide, returning to a sea that shouldn't exist. Water floods the basin and reveals a cave mouth. Inside, timbers, barnacles, a nameplate: Meridian Lark. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Thief in the Hold
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. She's been living aboard the wreck for weeks, searching for something specific. Odile corners her; she doesn't run. She says she's looking for what his mother left him. Emotional beat: confrontation flipping into alliance neither wants.

chapters.title: Coldharbour Papers
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In the captain's cabin they find a sealed strongbox bearing Odile's family name. Vess confesses her theft: she stole the compass that points here — his mother's compass. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Sails on the Salt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Salvage ships appear on the flooded basin — the fleet has found the wreck too. Their enforcer Harrow Quill is a man Odile knows too well: the mentor who raised him after his mother died. Emotional beat: old love weaponized.

chapters.title: Concession and Consequence
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Quill presents forged concession permits claiming fleet rights to the wreck. Privately he offers Odile a place at his side and warns him away from the strongbox. Emotional beat: the mentor's tenderness laced with threat.

chapters.title: The Compass Points Down
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The strongbox is locked and keyed to the compass itself. Vess reveals the debt's true origin: Odile's mother paid Vess's father to hide this ship, and the debt was meant to bring Odile here. Emotional beat: revelation as vertigo.

chapters.title: First Tide Lost
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fleet divers begin stripping the wreck legally. Odile tries to stall them with ranger authority and fails; his jurisdiction ends at the waterline. Six tides become five. Emotional beat: helplessness sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Bargain with the Bosun
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess bribes a disgruntled bosun, Tam Osk, for access to the hold — and learns Quill ordered the wreck scuttled with explosives once stripped. Emotional beat: fear becoming urgency.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Under cover of dark, Odile and Vess breach the captain's cabin while the fleet sleeps. They crack the strongbox using the compass as key. Inside: documents proving the concession was forged, signed by Quill himself. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Him Stars
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Odile's POV. Memory of childhood with Quill: lessons in navigation, in honor, in the lie that Odile's mother abandoned him. Understanding now how thoroughly Quill shaped his past. Emotional beat: mourning a living man.

chapters.title: Betrayal at Low Water
chapters.summary: Tam Osk's POV. Tam sells them out to Quill for a pardon. Quill takes the documents but lets Odile live — a mercy that is also a message. Four tides remain. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out.

chapters.title: Prisoner of the Permits
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Held on the flagship until the permits finalize, Odile plays compliant while memorizing the fleet's schedule and the location of the document copies Quill hasn't found. Emotional beat: patience as a blade being honed.

chapters.title: What Vess Never Stole
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Free and hunted, Vess recovers the second copy hidden in the compass's false back — the thing she was truly sent to find. She must decide whether to save herself or Odile. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against survival.

chapters.title: The Wreck Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Divers open a sealed compartment: remains of the crew, including records showing the Meridian Lark sailed with a fleet charter Quill countersigned — then sank deliberately. The forgery runs deeper than permits. Emotional beat: horror at scale.

chapters.title: Escape on the Fifth Tide
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess returns, cuts Odile out during a storm-tide chaos, and they flee across the flooding basin in a stolen skiff with the evidence. Tam hesitates at the critical moment and lets them go. Emotional beat: desperate, exhilarating flight.

chapters.title: The Hearing at High Water
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. At the port authority's emergency session, with one tide left, Odile presents the documents. Quill counters with charm and forged counter-evidence. It comes down to testimony — and Tam Osk walks in. Emotional beat: the scales trembling.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Lie
chapters.summary: Quill's POV. Cornered, Quill offers Odile one last bargain: burn the papers and inherit everything, the fleet, the name, the future. Odile sees the truth — Quill loved him, but loved control more. Emotional beat: severing the deepest bond.

chapters.title: Sixth Tide
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The final tide rises; the permits expire at slack water. Tam's testimony lands, the concessions void, and Quill orders the demolition charges fired anyway — but the wreck, already stripped of its secrets, is all he can destroy. Emotional beat: fury burning down to ash.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Quill arrested by the port authority he deceived; the wreck declared public heritage. Odile stands on the cave rim as the sea withdraws one last time, taking the Meridian Lark back. Emotional beat: release; the debt paid in truth rather than silence.

chapters.title: A Compass with No North
chapters.summary: Odile and Vess's alternating POV. Epilogue: Vess keeps the compass; Odile keeps the papers' story. They part at the edge of the desert — or don't quite. The basin dries, the legend begins. Emotional beat: quiet hope, an open horizon.
